settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: How the pharmacy works, and what it shows
settings.businessNameHint: Printed at the top of every receipt.
settings.npwpHint: Only needed once the business is a PKP.
settings.receiptLocaleHint: A business decision, not the cashier's. A cashier working in English must not hand an Indonesian customer an English receipt.
settings.timezoneHint: Decides when a day starts, which decides when a batch expires and which day a sale belongs to.
settings.modulesHint: This decides what staff are shown, not what they are allowed to do. Permissions remain the control, and nothing already recorded is hidden.

module.returnsHint: Taking medicine back over the counter. Off hides the returns screen and the button on a sale.
module.barcodesHint: The scan fields on receiving and at the till. Worth leaving off until a scanner is plugged in.
module.taxHint: Off means no tax fields anywhere and a plain nota. A pharmacy below the PKP threshold does not charge PPN.
module.narkotikaHint: Switch on the day you first stock them. Items already carrying these classes keep showing them either way.
module.suppliersHint: Supplier records and the picker on receiving. Off hides the Suppliers screen from the menu.
module.categoriesHint: Item categories, for organizing and filtering the catalogue. Off hides the Categories screen from the menu.
module.countsHint: Physical counts and posting the difference found. Off hides the Counts screen from the menu.
module.disposeHint: Recording expired or damaged stock as a loss. Off hides the Dispose screen from the menu.
module.importHint: The Import button on the Catalogue screen. Who may actually use it is still controlled by the "Import catalogue" permission per account.

settings.taxRateHistoryHint: Old rates are kept, never edited: a receipt reprinted from last year must still show the rate that applied on the day.
settings.noEffectiveRate: PPN is switched on but no rate covers today, so sales are being recorded with no PPN at all. Add a rate below.
settings.alertsHint: In days. Expired stock and out-of-stock are not thresholds — they are facts, and they always alert.
settings.allowRestock: Allow sealed stock back on the shelf
settings.allowRestockHint: Applies to over-the-counter items and devices only. Obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are always quarantined, whatever this says.
settings.restricted: Only the owner can change these.
settings.businessTaglineHint: The line under the name, on the sidebar and the sign-in screen. Describe the pharmacy, not the software.
settings.timezoneMismatch: This machine is set to {zone}. If that is where the pharmacy is, change this to match — an hour's difference moves a sale into the wrong day.
settings.digestHint: One email each morning with yesterday's takings and anything that needs attention before opening.
settings.digestEnabledHint: Nothing is sent until this is on and a mail server is configured below.
settings.digestHourHint: Local time. The job runs once a day; it does not send twice for the same day.
settings.digestPreviewOnly: No mail server is configured, so the digest is written to a file instead of sent. You can read it before deciding to switch sending on.
settings.mailHint: Used only for the daily digest. Leave it blank and the digest is written to a file you can open in a browser.
settings.smtpHostHint: For a Gmail address this is smtp.gmail.com, and the password is an app password rather than your own.
settings.smtpPasswordHint: Stored on the server and never shown again.
settings.smtpPasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave blank to keep it; type a new one to replace it.
settings.smtpFromHint: The address the email appears to come from. Most servers require it to be one you own.
settings.smtpSecureHint: On for port 465. Port 587 upgrades the connection itself and does not need this.
settings.mailTestHint: Connects and signs in without sending anything. Tests what is saved, so save first.
settings.mailFailed: Could not connect or sign in.
settings.demoHint: This installation still holds its starting demo catalogue: {items} items, {batches} batches and {sales} sales. It is there so staff can learn the till before real stock exists. Clear it on the day you begin the opening count.
settings.demoWiped: Demo data cleared. The catalogue, stock and history are empty; accounts and settings are untouched.
settings.demoKeeps: Accounts, permissions, settings, tax rates and the audit log all survive. Items, stock, the ledger, sales, returns, disposals, counts and alerts do not.

prompt.title: New here?
prompt.body: Take a two-minute walkthrough of the screens set up for your account.

intro.title: Welcome
intro.owner: This walkthrough covers every screen in the pharmacy system, since your account holds every permission. You can reopen it any time from this button.
intro.staff: This walkthrough only covers the screens set up for your account -- if something you use is missing here, ask the owner about your permissions. You can reopen it any time from this button.

chapters.dashboard: The first screen after signing in: what needs attention today, at a glance.
chapters.sell: Scan or search for an item, add it to the sale, and take payment. An expired batch is refused automatically, never just flagged.
chapters.items: The medicine catalogue: names, prices and drug classes. Stock itself lives on batches, not here, so quantities are never edited from this screen.
chapters.receive: Record a delivery from a supplier. Each delivery becomes its own batch, with its own expiry date and cost, so stock and cost tracking stay accurate down to the lot.
chapters.sales: Every past sale, with its receipt. A sale can be voided here where that is still allowed -- not once it has been returned against.
chapters.returns: Process a customer return. Returned medicine is quarantined rather than put straight back on the shelf, and controlled classes are never resold at all.
chapters.dispose: Record expired or damaged stock leaving inventory as a loss, kept separate from ordinary corrections so the expiry-loss report stays honest.
chapters.counts: Do a physical stock count and post the difference the count found, rather than overwriting what the system has on hand.
chapters.alerts: Expiring batches, low stock and other warnings. Critical alerts, like expired stock still on the shelf, cannot be snoozed by anyone.
chapters.suppliers: Keep supplier names and contact details for use when receiving stock.
chapters.categories: Group items into categories to keep the catalogue and reports organised.
chapters.reports: What sold, and -- for those with permission to see cost prices -- what it cost and what it made.
chapters.users: Create staff accounts, set what each one can do, and issue or reset passwords.
chapters.settings: The pharmacy's name, timezone, tax rate and which optional screens are switched on.

outro.title: That's everything
outro.body: You can come back to this walkthrough any time using the Tutorial button.
